pr_title: fix(common): reflect input type in context
pr_body:
Fixes `NgForOf` not reflecting the type of its input in the `NgForOfContext`. Also fixes `NgIf` which was typed to `any`.

Fixes #33527.
Fixes #31556.
pr_comments: also, this should target the 9.0.x branch as well because otherwise we won't be able to roll this out until v10. (I updated the target label)
I've addressed the feedback. Can you take another look @JoostK @IgorMinar?
I have all the feedback addressed locally, but it uncovered some issues with the new signatures. I'll pair up with Joost tomorrow.
All the issues and feedback should addressed now. Thank you for the help with the tests @JoostK!

It seems like there should be a test for how this typing behaves with `*ngIf="something | async; let thing"`. In that case, the behavior here doesn't seem to align with one of the most common use cases of `*ngIf`.

review_comments: We are missing the most important change here: `NgForOfContext` also needs the `U extends NgIterable<T>` type parameter, as we can then flow the type from `dir: NgForOf<T, U>` into the `NgForOfContext<T, U>` return type here. Then, `NgForOfContext.ngForOf` can be of type `U`, so that any reads from that property will be inferred as `Array<T>` or `Iterable<T>`, instead of `NgIterable<T>`.

There's currently nothing that allows for inferring the type `T` from the condition variable, which would be the `ngIf` input. Then, to allow the inferred type `T` to flow into `NgIfContext<T>` we'd need a `ngTemplateContextGuard` similar to that of `NgForOf`.
